title_en: Zhang Yi v. Zheng Zhongwei and China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., Wuhan Branch — dispute over condominium ownership
ruling_gist_en: In adjudicating cases concerning disputes over partitioned ownership of buildings, even if the owner's use of the premises does not cause noise, sewage, odors, or other impacts on other partitioned owners, as long as the purpose of the premises has changed from exclusive personal and family daily residential use to commercial, industrial, tourism, office, or other operational activities, it may be determined that such conduct has affected the peaceful life of the owners, constituting a conversion of residential use to commercial use. The matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 77 of the Property Law regarding the change of residential use by owners.
keywords_en: Civil law; Dispute over partitioned ownership of buildings; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Hubei Province; Natural person; Legal person; Property Law; Determination of conversion of residential use to commercial use; Consent of interested owners; Exemption for public welfare purposes; Reversal of judgment; Conversion of residence to communication equipment room; Fiber optic transmission equipment; Opposition by owners; Property rights; Dispute over partitioned ownership of buildings involving a company
full_text_en:
Zhang Yi v. Zheng Zhongwei and China United Network Communications Co., Ltd. Wuhan Branch
— Dispute over Condominium Ownership

### 【Ruling Summary】

In hearing cases concerning condominium ownership, even if an owner's use of a unit does not cause noise, sewage, odors, or other impacts on other unit owners, a change in the nature of the unit—from being exclusively used for personal or family daily living to being used for commercial, industrial, tourism, office, or other business activities—may be deemed to affect the peaceful living of the owners. Such a change constitutes the conversion of residential premises into business premises and shall be handled in accordance with Article 77 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China regarding the alteration of the purpose of residential premises by the owner.

Where a user of premises (other than the owner) converts residential premises into business premises, such user shall bear the same legal obligations as the owner, which include, in addition to complying with laws, regulations, and the management covenant, obtaining the consent of the interested owners.

Plaintiff: Zhang Yi, male, 31 years old, Han Chinese, residing at Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City.

Defendant: Zheng Zhongwei, male, 37 years old, Han Chinese, residing at Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City.

Defendant: China United Network Communications Co., Ltd. Wuhan Branch, domiciled at Jin Yin Hu Ma Chi Road, Dongxihu District, Wuhan City.

The Plaintiff, Zhang Yi, filed a lawsuit with the Wuchang District People's Court of Wuhan City, Hubei Province, against the Defendants, Zheng Zhongwei and China United Network Communications Co., Ltd. Wuhan Branch (hereinafter referred to as "China Unicom Wuhan Branch"), concerning a dispute over condominium ownership.

Plaintiff Zhang Yi alleged: The Defendant Zheng Zhongwei is the owner of Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City. In December 2011, without the consent of the interested owners within the residential community, the Defendant Zheng Zhongwei and the Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch arbitrarily installed fiber-optic transmission cabinets, power supply cabinets, storage batteries, and other equipment in Unit A, converting Unit A into a communication equipment room. This equipment room operates 24 hours a day without any personnel on duty, posing a safety hazard. The relevant owners and the property management office of White Rose Garden repeatedly advised both Defendants to stop, but both Defendants ignored these requests. The Plaintiff now brings this action to the court, requesting an order that both Defendants remove the fiber-optic transmission equipment located in Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City, restore the premises to residential use, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

The Plaintiff Zhang Yi submitted the following evidence:

1.  A property registration information inquiry form, proving that the Defendant Zheng Zhongwei is the owner of Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, and that the designed purpose of the premises is residential.
2.  A copy of the House Ownership Certificate (Wuhan Real Estate Certificate Hong Zi No. 2007010794), proving that the Plaintiff Zhang Yi's residential unit is located directly below the Defendant Zheng Zhongwei's unit, and that the Plaintiff is an interested owner in this case.
3.  Five photographs, a statement regarding China Unicom's installation of fiber-optic transmission equipment in White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, and a notice of discontinuation/restriction of electricity supply due to unauthorized electricity theft/irregularities, proving that fiber-optic transmission equipment is installed in Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, that China Unicom has converted it into a communication equipment room, and that the Defendant Zheng Zhongwei uses a 380-volt non-residential power supply in Unit A.
4.  Testimonies of witnesses Ye Guojun and Ma Zhanjun, proving that the witnesses are interested owners of units in the same building as Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, and that they do not consent to the conversion of Unit A into business premises and request the removal of the relevant fiber-optic transmission equipment.
5.  A notice of discontinuation/restriction of electricity supply due to unauthorized electricity theft/irregularities obtained by the court upon the Plaintiff Zhang Yi's application from the Wuchang Power Supply Business Office of Wuhan Wuchang Power Supply Company.

Defendant Zheng Zhongwei argued: Zheng Zhongwei is the owner of Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road. Pursuant to relevant laws and regulations, he enjoys the rights to use and dispose of this unit. Leasing the unit to China Unicom Wuhan Branch was lawful and reasonable, and did not cause harm to other owners or pose any safety hazard. The property management office of White Rose Garden did issue a rectification notice, but we consider it invalid. Other public service companies have installed equipment in the common areas owned by all owners of White Rose Garden, whereas China Unicom's equipment is placed only within my own unit and does not occupy any common area. The Plaintiff's claim should be dismissed in accordance with the law, and the Plaintiff should bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch argued: Pursuant to the Telecommunications Regulations and the Property Law, after signing a lease agreement with the Defendant Zheng Zhongwei, China Unicom Wuhan Branch has the right to install telecommunications equipment. The room where China Unicom Wuhan Branch installed the telecommunications equipment does not constitute business premises and has not had any impact on the lives of the residents of the community. The Plaintiff Zhang Yi's claim should be dismissed in accordance with the law.

First Instance Findings of the Wuchang District People's Court of Wuhan City, Hubei Province:

The Defendant Zheng Zhongwei obtained the house ownership certificate for Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City (hereinafter referred to as "Unit A"), with a designed purpose of residential, on April 28, 2003. Zhang Yi obtained the house ownership certificate for Unit B, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City, with a designed purpose of residential, in 2007. Zheng Zhongwei and Zhang Yi are neighbors living on different floors in the same building unit.

The Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch signed a contract for the construction, operation, maintenance, and lease of the Wuhan City Video Surveillance System Project with the Wuhan Public Security Bureau and others on May 13, 2010.

Liu Baojiao (the sister-in-law of the Defendant Zheng Zhongwei) signed a lease contract for the White Rose Garden communication equipment room with the Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch on October 8, 2011, stipulating that China Unicom Wuhan Branch would use Unit A to build a communication equipment room, with the lease term from October 8, 2011 to October 7, 2015, and an annual rent of RMB 29,800. Liu Baojiao was responsible for coordinating with surrounding residents to ensure normal construction and daily maintenance by China Unicom Wuhan Branch. China Unicom Wuhan Branch guaranteed that the renovation and decoration of the premises would not affect the structural safety of the building, and that the equipment during operation or due to aging would not affect the lives and rest of surrounding residents.

The Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch took possession and began using Unit A in December 2011. At the same time, Zheng Zhongliang, the brother of Zheng Zhongwei, continued to reside and use Unit A.

Starting from March 19, 2012, the White Rose Garden property management office and the owners of White Rose Garden repeatedly requested the owner of Unit A to "cease production and business operations, restore the premises to residential use, and eliminate safety hazards."

The Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch obtained the Wuhan Major Project Certification Certificate on April 8, 2012, indicating the project name as Wireless City Comprehensive Project—"China Unicom Wireless City," valid until April 8, 2014.

Wuhan Wuchang Power Supply Company issued a notice of discontinuation/restriction of electricity supply due to unauthorized electricity theft/irregularities on July 17, 2012, finding that the owner of Unit A was using high-voltage electricity under a low-voltage rate.

The Defendant China Unicom Wuhan Branch installed fiber-optic transmission cabinets in Unit A as data transmission aggregation nodes to build a wired fiber-optic broadband network, addressing the aggregation and switching needs for "Safe City" video surveillance recording transmission, the Wireless City Comprehensive Project WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network), and broadband and fixed-line telephone access services for surrounding residential communities.

The Plaintiff Zhang Yi filed this lawsuit against the Defendants Zheng Zhongwei and China Unicom Wuhan Branch on January 16, 2013, requesting an order that Zheng Zhongwei and China Unicom Wuhan Branch remove the fiber-optic transmission equipment located in Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City, and restore the premises to residential use.

First Instance Opinion of the Wuchang District People's Court of Wuhan City, Hubei Province:

The nature of this case is a dispute over condominium ownership. The legislative purpose of Article 77 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China is primarily aimed at the use of residential premises for commercial production, large-scale catering, entertainment, bathing, or office use, which typically causes noise, sewage, odors, excessive entry and exit of outsiders, and other impacts affecting the peaceful living of other unit owners. In other words, not every change of use of residential premises falls within the scope regulated by Article 77 of the Property Law. The Defendants Zheng Zhongwei and China Unicom Wuhan Branch did not change the residential nature of the subject premises; even if they did, it was for public welfare purposes. Moreover, the Plaintiff Zhang Yi failed to provide evidence that the value or quality of life of his own premises had been or might be adversely affected. Therefore, the Plaintiff's claim is not supported.

Accordingly, the Wuchang District People's Court, pursuant to Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered judgment on September 26, 2013:

Rejecting the Plaintiff Zhang Yi's claim.

Zhang Yi appealed the first-instance judgment to the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province, arguing:

1.  The first-instance judgment omitted significant facts and erred in fact-finding. The Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch submitted as evidence (Exhibit 4) the Construction, Operation, Maintenance, and Lease Contract for the Wuhan City Video Surveillance System Project dated May 13, 2012, with a contract amount as high as hundreds of millions of yuan. The first-instance judgment omitted this significant fact, leading to the erroneous finding that the Appellees Zheng Zhongwei and China Unicom Wuhan Branch did not change the residential nature of the disputed premises, or that any change was for public welfare purposes. The Appellee Zheng Zhongwei submitted as evidence (Exhibit 2) two photos dated March 25, 2013, showing only some daily necessities. The first-instance court used this evidence to find that Zheng Zhongliang, the brother of Zheng Zhongwei, had been residing in Room 302, which is an error in fact-finding.

2.  The first-instance judgment arbitrarily engaged in judicial interpretation, which is clearly illegal. The first-instance court erroneously interpreted the legislative purpose of Article 77 of the Property Law as being primarily aimed at business activities that affect the peaceful living of unit owners. However, under the Legislation Law of the People's Republic of China, the power of legal interpretation belongs to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The interpretation by the first-instance court violates the provisions of the Legislation Law.

3.  The actions of the two Appellees have seriously infringed the rights of interested owners. The people's court should order immediate removal to eliminate the hazard.

In summary, the Appellant requests: (1) Reversal of the first-instance judgment and remand for retrial, or modification of the judgment after ascertaining the facts; (2) An order that the two Appellees remove the fiber-optic transmission equipment located in Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, and restore the premises to residential use.

The Appellant Zhang Yi submitted one piece of evidence in the second instance: a civil appeal petition, proving that all owners opposed the actions of the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch.

The Appellee Zheng Zhongwei argued:

1.  Zheng Zhongwei's leasing of his self-owned property to the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch was lawful and reasonable. The Property Law grants owners the rights of possession, use, and enjoyment of their own movable or immovable property.

2.  The first-instance judgment was fair and reasonable. The first-instance court's interpretation of Article 77 of the Property Law was correct. No existing law prohibits the Appellee from leasing his premises to China Unicom Wuhan Branch for installing fiber-optic equipment.

3.  The Appellee not only submitted photos in the first instance to prove that the premises could be normally inhabited, but the first-instance court judges also personally inspected the disputed premises, confirming that someone was living there.

4.  The Appellant Zhang Yi claims that China Unicom Wuhan Branch infringed his rights, but has not provided evidence of what specific rights were violated. China Unicom Wuhan Branch hired professionals to test for radiation, and no radiation was detected, but the Appellant does not believe this result.

5.  There are other communication equipment in the public areas of the community. If the communication equipment in the Appellee's home is to be removed, other communication equipment in the public areas should also be removed.

In summary, the Appellee requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The Appellee Zheng Zhongwei submitted one piece of evidence in the second instance: a set of invoices for water, electricity, and gas for the past year, proving that someone has been residing in the disputed premises.

The Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch argued: The Appellant Zhang Yi has a partial understanding of the concept of public welfare. China Unicom Wuhan Branch's situation is similar to that of power companies or water supply companies; although they charge users fees, they are still providing public welfare services. The Appellee requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch submitted one piece of evidence in the second instance: a notice from the General Office of the Wuhan Municipal People's Government on Further Strengthening the Construction of Wireless Cities, proving that the Wuhan Municipal People's Government requires all sectors of society to support infrastructure construction and wireless city construction, and to strictly implement the national standards for "Design Specifications for Fiber-to-the-Home Communication Facilities in Residential Areas and Residential Buildings" and "Construction and Acceptance Specifications for Fiber-to-the-Home Communication Facilities in Residential Areas and Residential Buildings."

Second Instance Findings of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province:

After the second instance, the court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Additionally, it was found that the Appellee Zheng Zhongwei acknowledged the lease contract for the White Rose Garden communication equipment room signed by Liu Baojiao with the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch on October 8, 2011. The Construction, Operation, Maintenance, and Lease Contract for the Wuhan City Video Surveillance System Project signed by China Unicom Wuhan Branch with the Wuhan Public Security Bureau on May 13, 2010, stipulated that the contract benchmark price, i.e., the winning bid price of China Unicom Wuhan Branch and Jinpeng Electronic Information Machine Co., Ltd. during the procurement process, was RMB 186 million.

The issues for determination in the second instance were:

1.  Whether the act of the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch in installing fiber-optic transmission cabinets as data transmission aggregation nodes in the disputed premises constitutes the conversion of residential premises into business premises.

2.  If the above act of China Unicom Wuhan Branch constitutes the conversion of residential premises into business premises, whether it should have obtained the consent of the Appellant Zhang Yi.

Second Instance Opinion of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province:

1. Regarding the first issue.

The act of the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch in installing fiber-optic transmission cabinets as data transmission aggregation nodes in the disputed premises constitutes the conversion of residential premises into business premises. The reasons are as follows: Residential premises refer to units exclusively used for the daily living of individuals and families. Business premises refer to units used for commercial, industrial, tourism, office, and other business activities. The two are fundamentally different in purpose. The primary use of residential premises is for living; the primary use of business premises is for business activities. In this case, China Unicom Wuhan Branch leased the disputed premises to install fiber-optic transmission cabinets as data transmission aggregation nodes, to build a wired fiber-optic broadband network, addressing the aggregation and switching needs for "Safe City" video surveillance recording transmission, the Wireless City Comprehensive Project WLAN, and broadband and fixed-line telephone access services for surrounding residential communities. From this purpose, it is clear that the lease of the disputed premises was not for living but for engaging in business activities. Therefore, the above act of China Unicom Wuhan Branch constitutes the conversion of residential premises into business premises.

2. Regarding the second issue.

The act of the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch in installing fiber-optic transmission cabinets as data transmission aggregation nodes in the disputed premises should have obtained the consent of the Appellant Zhang Yi. The reasons are as follows:

First, an owner who converts residential premises into business premises must obtain the consent of the interested owners. According to Article 77 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, "An owner shall not, in violation of laws, regulations, and the management covenant, convert residential premises into business premises. Where an owner converts residential premises into business premises, in addition to complying with laws, regulations, and the management covenant, the owner shall obtain the consent of the interested owners." Therefore, the legality of converting residential premises into business premises requires the satisfaction of two conditions: (1) Compliance with laws, regulations, and the management covenant; and (2) Obtaining the consent of the interested owners. Even if there is no violation of laws, regulations, or the management covenant, the conversion of residential premises into business premises is still not lawful if the consent of the interested owners has not been obtained. The wording of Article 77 of the Property Law is clear and its meaning is unambiguous. The first-instance court's restrictive interpretation of "owner converting residential premises into business premises" in that article was improper and is hereby corrected. Pursuant to Article 10, Paragraph 1, of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Cases Involving Disputes over Condominium Ownership: "Where an owner converts residential premises into business premises without obtaining the consent of the interested owners as required by Article 77 of the Property Law, and an interested owner requests removal of the nuisance, elimination of danger, restoration to original condition, or compensation for losses, the people's court shall support such request." And Article 16, Paragraph 1, of the same Interpretation: "Where a dispute over condominium ownership involves a lessee, borrower, or other user of an exclusive part, this Interpretation shall apply mutatis mutandis." As a lessee of the disputed premises, China Unicom Wuhan Branch, in converting residential premises into business premises, shall bear the same legal obligations as the owner, and therefore must also obtain the consent of the interested owners.

Second, the Appellant Zhang Yi shall be deemed an interested owner. According to Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Cases Involving Disputes over Condominium Ownership: "Where an owner converts residential premises into business premises, other owners within the same building shall be deemed 'interested owners' as referred to in Article 77 of the Property Law. Owners outside the same building within the building division who claim to have an interest shall bear the burden of proving that the value or quality of life of their premises has been or may be adversely affected." As an owner within the same building, the Appellant Zhang Yi is deemed an interested owner without needing to prove that the value or quality of life of his premises has been or may be adversely affected.

In conclusion, the act of the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch in leasing the premises of the Appellee Zheng Zhongwei to install fiber-optic transmission cabinets as data transmission aggregation nodes constitutes the conversion of residential premises into business premises. This act did not obtain the consent of the interested owner, the Appellant Zhang Yi. Pursuant to the aforementioned Article 10, Paragraph 1, and Article 16, Paragraph 1, of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation, China Unicom Wuhan Branch shall bear corresponding liability. The Appellee Zheng Zhongwei, knowing that his sister-in-law Liu Baojiao leased the disputed premises to the Appellee China Unicom Wuhan Branch for building a communication equipment room, nevertheless ratified the lease contract. Therefore, he shall bear joint liability with China Unicom Wuhan Branch. Accordingly, the Appellant Zhang Yi's request on appeal—that Zheng Zhongwei and China Unicom Wuhan Branch remove the fiber-optic transmission equipment located in Unit A, [X] Building, [X] Unit, White Rose Garden, Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, and restore the premises to residential use—is supported. The first-instance judgment correctly found the facts but improperly applied the law. Therefore, the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered judgment on January 20, 2014:

1. Reversing the Civil Judgment (2013) E Wu Chang Min Chu Zi No. 00444 of the Wuchang District People's Court of Wuhan City;

2. Zheng Zhongwei and China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., Wuhan Branch shall, within sixty days after this judgment takes effect, remove the optical fiber transmission equipment located at the premises of Room A, Unit X, Building X, Bai Mei Gui Hua Yuan (White Rose Garden), Zhongbei Road, Wuchang District, Wuhan City, and restore the premises to residential use.

This judgment is final.
